acceptance: A regression test reproduces the v0.5.55 failure: a full https Git repository URL with a stale tag-tree release.json must resolve the immutable release asset metadata rather than fail before installer writes.

The public installer keeps fail-closed verification and accepts only a normalized canonical repository identity when deriving the immutable release asset URL; malformed or unsupported repositories still fail.
The v0.5.56 candidate remains the sole next patch after immutable v0.5.55 and its source version, state, and release evidence checks remain consistent.
The merged source Work Item preserves the public-main failure as a successor release requirement; no immutable tag or Issue #783 state changes occur here.
guidelines: Do not replace a failed metadata verification with a bypass, caller-provided trust root, cache hit, or mutable main metadata.
Preserve exact tag/source/archive/installer/release-digests binding before any adopter writes.
Do not claim delivery until the published public entrypoint succeeds in a fresh repository and all release gates are green.

intent.problem: Post-merge public verification reproduced a real future-adopter failure: main/release.json correctly selected v0.5.55, but the v0.5.55 tagged installer received a full public Git URL and could not normalize it to the release asset metadata URL. It therefore read the stale v0.5.54 tag-tree release.json and failed closed before any installation writes.
constraints: Repair the metadata asset fallback at the installer trust boundary, retain fail-closed behavior, and prepare only the next legal patch candidate v0.5.56.
Preserve v0.5.50 through v0.5.55 immutable history and all validation, coverage, security, release, and installer gates.
A successor release Work Item must use same-SHA rehearsal, public provider assets, fresh public-main discovery, and a clean adopter installation as release evidence.
Record the user approval below and complete this source PR merge; do not create a release from an unmerged branch.
intent.rationale: The installer repair must be merged before a successor can create the immutable release that delivers the performance benefit; this preserves the repository's PR-first release lifecycle.
